rules.title: California Driver's Handbook — Knowledge-Test Device Rule
rules.summary: Applicants may not use testing aids during a knowledge test; a cell phone is expressly listed as an example. This is examination-specific and cannot be generalized into a branch-wide no-phone or no-camera rule.
rules.constitutional_test: Purpose-limited examination channel; any extension beyond test-taking requires separate authority and constitutional analysis.
rules.enforcement_hook: DMV test administration rules; no branch-wide recording hook established.
open_questions: What branch instructions exist for phones/cameras outside an active test?

rules.title: DMV Privacy and Security Policy
rules.summary: Identifies DMV duties concerning sensitive personal information. It is not by itself a public camera prohibition.
rules.constitutional_test: Use as asserted privacy interest; any visitor restriction must be separately sourced and tested.
rules.enforcement_hook: Agency information-security obligations, not a visitor camera offense.
open_questions: What physical safeguards and staff instructions govern exposed information at public counters?

rules.title: DMV Information Disclosure / Record-Protection Rules
rules.summary: Describes protected categories and disclosure limits. These obligations help identify legitimate privacy interests but do not themselves create a general customer camera ban.
rules.constitutional_test: Facility privacy duty must be separated from visitor conduct restrictions.
rules.enforcement_hook: Underlying privacy statutes/regulations govern DMV disclosure.

rules.title: Vehicle Code §1808.5 — Physical/Mental Condition Records
rules.summary: Makes specified DMV records confidential. It governs protected records; it does not by text create a general camera prohibition in the waiting room.
rules.constitutional_test: Privacy-context authority; a visitor restriction requires separate legal basis.

rules.title: California Information Practices Act
rules.summary: Regulates state-agency collection/use/disclosure of personal information. It is context for DMV's safeguard duty, not a standalone visitor camera ban.
rules.constitutional_test: Separate agency privacy duty from visitor restriction.

rules.title: Driver's Privacy Protection Act
rules.summary: Restricts disclosure/use of qualifying motor-vehicle record information. It does not itself establish a blanket no-recording rule for a DMV customer lobby.
rules.constitutional_test: Use as privacy/confidentiality context only unless conduct falls within statutory scope.

rules.title: California Penal Code §632 — Confidential Communications
rules.summary: Can directly restrict recording where the communication is objectively confidential and statutory elements are met. It is not a blanket indoor-audio rule.
rules.constitutional_test: Statutory elements + First Amendment analysis where protected recording is burdened.
open_questions: Which counter interactions, if any, objectively satisfy confidentiality requirements?

rules.title: California Trespass / Public-Agency Obstruction Statutes
rules.summary: The statewide California removal, trespass, and public-agency-obstruction framework is now researched. At this facility, the live question is which actual rule, Title 13 predicate, order, and statutory branch apply to the specific facts.
rules.constitutional_test: Exact statutory elements + constitutional savings clause + validity of underlying restriction/exclusion
rules.enforcement_hook: Penal Code §§602/602.1 only where their elements are satisfied.
open_questions: Which subsection/policy does DMV/security actually invoke in recording-related removals?

rules.title: Title 13 CCR ch. 11 — Applicability to State Property
applies_to: state-owned/leased/controlled property, including DMV field-office property unless an exclusion applies
rules.summary: Chapter 11 expressly applies to individuals/groups using broadly defined state property. CHP's current State Property Event Permits manual expressly gives DMV field-office events as an implementation example. This is a previously missing statewide rule layer for the Concord DMV.
rules.constitutional_test: Use Chapter 11 as the actual regulatory source, then test each substantive restriction under the exact forum/activity standard.
rules.enforcement_hook: Substantive enforcement depends on the specific Chapter 11 provision and other statutory authority.
open_questions: Which CHP field Division/Area SOP governs permit processing for Concord DMV?
Which exact DMV parcel/subareas are treated as state property for Chapter 11 purposes?

rules.title: Title 13 CCR §§1855 & 1860 — Demonstration/Gathering and Structure Permit
applies_to: tables/booths/platforms/sound systems and other listed structures
rules.summary: Chapter 11 requires a permit for a defined 'demonstration' or 'gathering' on state property and for listed structures/equipment. Applications are directed to CHP at least ten business days in advance. The definitions cover expressive activity capable of drawing a crowd and gatherings of more than two persons meeting the stated criteria. At DMV's NPF-classified facility-controlled areas this receives more governmental latitude than a TPF, but the advance-permit requirement and its application to spontaneous or low-impact expression still require constitutional testing.
rules.constitutional_test: NPF reasonableness + viewpoint neutrality for DMV-controlled NPF areas; do not export this rule to independently established municipal TPF sidewalk/ROW
rules.enforcement_hook: Title 13 permit requirements; implementation through CHP state-property permit process.
open_questions: Whether CHP/DMV treats small or spontaneous expressive activity at Concord DMV as requiring a permit.
What local SOP, alternative location, or expedited practice exists when ten-business-day advance application is impossible.
Whether the regulation is ever applied to a single peaceful recorder rather than a defined demonstration/gathering.

rules.title: Title 13 CCR §1861 — Grounds for Order to Leave State Property
rules.summary: This regulation is important because it does not say an employee may order a lawful visitor off state property for any reason. Its text conditions the leave order on enumerated findings: disruptive loud/unusual noise, obstruction/interference or a health/safety hazard, presence when closed without lawful reason, or refusal of an emergency order. That is a materially narrower public rule than 'staff told you to leave, therefore trespass.'
rules.constitutional_test: First determine whether a listed §1861 predicate actually exists; then test any expressive application under the governing forum and activity doctrine.
rules.enforcement_hook: Order to leave under §1861 only after the regulation's stated predicate determination.
open_questions: What DMV/CHP training defines 'person having charge of the facility' and documents the required determination?
What additional statute is used for citation/arrest after refusal?

rules.title: Title 13 CCR §1862 — Signs, Posters, Placards, Banners
rules.summary: The rule requires prior written permission for signs larger than 30 by 30 inches, restricts supports, requires signs to be hand-carried rather than affixed/self-supporting/leaned, and prohibits carrying signs that obstruct passage. Permission review for oversized signs is expressly stated not to be content-based. This is the actual statewide sign rule to analyze at DMV-controlled state property.
rules.constitutional_test: NPF reasonableness + viewpoint neutrality at DMV-controlled NPF areas; separate TPF analysis if activity occurs on a true municipal sidewalk/ROW outside state property
open_questions: How CHP/DMV communicates or enforces §1862 at Concord DMV.
Whether any local sign rule adds restrictions beyond §1862.

rules.title: California Driver's Handbook — Behind-the-Wheel Recording-Device Prohibition
rules.summary: DMV expressly prohibits use of a video/audio recording device during a behind-the-wheel drive test and requires a device that cannot be disabled to be blocked. This is a real current recording restriction, but it is test-specific; it does not establish a field-office lobby, waiting-area, counter, parking-lot, or general customer camera ban.
rules.constitutional_test: Purpose-limited examination activity + First Amendment recording analysis; scope must remain tied to the drive test rather than generalized to unrelated public-facing areas
rules.enforcement_hook: DMV drive-test administration rule; consequences beyond test administration require separate authority.
open_questions: What legal/policy source underlies the handbook restriction and what consequence is imposed for refusal?
Whether any local staff instruction improperly generalizes this test-only rule beyond the drive test.

cpra_targets.target: DMV statewide and Concord-specific internal directives, security instructions, training, customer-conduct guidance, or staff scripts governing public photography, video/audio recording, phone use, information gathering, privacy at counters, and requests to stop recording.
cpra_targets.why: No dedicated public-facing field-office camera rule was located. Internal implementation remains the most important gap for recording.

cpra_targets.target: Current sign templates/orders and Concord field-office sign inventory for entrance, waiting area, counters, knowledge-test stations, kiosk, parking, and approaches relating to cameras, phones, demonstrations, signs, privacy, conduct, or removal.
cpra_targets.why: The completeness sweep found substantial statewide rules but physical/local posted mandates remain unverified.

cpra_targets.target: DMV and/or responsible CHP Area guidance for implementing 13 CCR §§1855, 1860, 1861, and 1862 at DMV field offices, including the applicable field Division/Area SOP, who may act as 'person having charge,' and the citation/arrest authority used after a §1861 order.
cpra_targets.why: The regulation is now public and directly applicable, so CPRA should target implementation rather than asking whether a rule exists.

cpra_targets.target: Complaints/incidents during the last three years involving photography, recording, demonstrations, leafleting, petitioning, signs, or refusal to stop/leave at California DMV field offices, with the policy/regulation cited and disposition.
cpra_targets.why: Would show how Chapter 11 and any unpublished camera rules are actually used, including whether protected low-impact activity is being treated as prohibited.
